resale_co.name: Residential Certificate of Occupancy (Housing Code Section 55-13)
resale_co.issued_by: Gloucester City Housing and Building Department (Housing Inspector / Code Enforcement Official)
resale_co.valid_for: Until the next change of occupant or transfer of title; not transferable
requirements: Home must meet the New Jersey State Housing Code (City Code 55-12)
Hard-wired, interconnected smoke detectors with battery backup on or near the ceiling of each level, certified by the Fire Official
Battery smoke detectors in each bedroom or sleeping area
All utilities must be on for the inspection
Warrant waiver from the Gloucester City Municipal Court (313 Monmouth St) showing no outstanding warrants for the buyer, owner and proposed occupants
Proof of identity for buyer and tenants; for an LLC, partnership or corporation, the record owner's name, address and phone
All outstanding Housing Office fees on the property (including vacant/abandoned property fees) must be paid first
Violations must be fixed and reinspected within 90 days of the first report (one extension to 120 days if asked in time), or a new application and fee are needed

fees.label: Initial inspection including first re-inspection (2019 form)
Certificate for Transfer of Property Title, vacant property sale only (a CO application must follow within 90 days)
fees.quote: The fee for said certificate for transfer is $75.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for Residential Certificate of Occupancy (check "Sale"), take a copy to the Municipal Court at 313 Monmouth St for the warrant waiver, and turn it in with payment (check or cash) to the Housing and Building Department, 700 Somerset St, Gloucester City, NJ 08030 (drop slot or mail also accepted). Incomplete applications are not accepted. A vacant property can instead get a Certificate for Transfer of Property Title ($75, valid 90 days) if a CO application is filed before it expires.
resale_co.contact_title: Chief Housing Inspector and Zoning Official

resale_co.notes: Settled in round 3 from official City documents saved by the Internet Archive (the live cityofgloucester.org returns a Cloudflare bot check, which was not bypassed). City Code 55-13 requires the owner to get a certificate of occupancy from the Housing Inspector or Code Enforcement Official before any new occupant moves in and before title to improved property is transferred by purchase or otherwise; the City's June 2024 building-permits bulletin says all property owners must obtain a CO under Section 55-13. The code text is from the 12-31-2014 supplement and the fee amounts are from the Feb 2019 application (the code states the same amounts in words: one hundred dollars, fifteen dollars, fifty dollars). A current search listing (lead only, not verified) shows that Ordinance O18-2024 changed the wording in 55-13 from "Certificate of Occupancy" to "Certificate of Inspection", and that the current application still requires the Municipal Court warrant waiver; the fee may have changed since 2019. No lead time or validity period is published. Commercial COs have separate fees. Contact: William Ackley signed a 2020 Housing Department notice as Chief Housing Inspector and Zoning Officer and is listed as a key contact on the 2022 forms page; confirm he is still in the role. Office: 700 Somerset St.

authorities.name: Gloucester City Fire Department (Fire Official Patrick R. Hagan); DCA directory lists 'Gloucester City Housing' as the smoke detector compliance contact
authorities.how_to_apply: The City handles smoke detector certification with the Housing CO: City Code 55-13 says the CO is issued upon the Fire Official's certification of the smoke detectors, and the DCA directory lists Gloucester City Housing, 700 Somerset St (DCA lists 512 Monmouth St), (856) 456-7689, as the smoke detector compliance contact. No separate smoke/CO application or fee was found. Fire Official: Patrick R. Hagan, (856) 456-2652.

fire_cert.notes: The NJ DCA Uniform Fire Code registry (July 2026) lists Gloucester City with code F (Fire Department) as its local enforcing agency. City Code 55-13 C(1) ties the smoke detector certification to the Housing CO, and the DCA directory lists "Gloucester City Housing" (856-456-7689) as the smoke detector compliance contact, so in practice the smoke/CO certification appears to be done with the Housing CO inspection. The City's 2004 Fire Prevention chapter (Chapter 48, archived copy) lists annual registration fees and a $25.00 certificate of fire code status, but no smoke/CO certificate fee. A search summary in round 2 mentioned $45 / $90 / $161 and a $10 fee; no official text showing them was found, so none are recorded. A 2014 vacant-property Transfer of Title form required one battery smoke detector per level.

other_items.label: Municipal Court warrant waiver
other_items.detail: Take a copy of the CO application to the Gloucester City Municipal Court, 313 Monmouth St, for a warrant waiver for the buyer, owner and proposed occupants (City Code 55-13 D(4)).

other_items.label: Outstanding Housing Office fees
other_items.detail: Under Ordinance 019-2017, all fees owed to the City Housing Office on the property, including vacant or abandoned property fees, must be paid before a Certificate of Occupancy or Transfer of Title is issued (notice attached to the 2019 application).

other_items.label: Vacant property sale option
other_items.detail: A vacant structure can be transferred with a Certificate for Transfer of Property Title ($75, valid 90 days, one battery smoke detector per level), but a CO application must be filed before it expires.
